newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah softens on heated poll campaign.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah softens on heated poll campaign.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah softened against the dollar in moderate early trading on Monday on the back of the heated campaign for May 29 general elections.
One Japanese bank dealer said the rupiah was well supported at the opening as the dollar weakened against major currencies.
"But operators seem to resort to the election issue later and increased pressure on the rupiah," the dealer said.

On Sunday, tens of thousands of supporters from the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) and loyalists of the ousted chief of the rival Indonesian Democratic Party campaigned jointly and brought Jakarta to a virtual standstill.
There were also reports of sporadic clashes from Central Java, where the PPP was campaigning.

One U.S. bank dealer said liquidity worries had prevented players from making heavy dollar purchases despite attempts to factor in the political uncertainty which will last for another two weeks. The election campaign will last till May 23.
Spot rupiah was at 2,427.75/28.25 at 0345 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,426.5/27.5. Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,427.25/27.75 and 2,426.50/27.25, respectively.
"The tone is a bit biddish on the dollar. But people are still worried about possible tightening on Tuesday due to weekly tax payments," the U.S. bank dealer said.

Dealers said swap rates edged up on the back of slight liquidity tightening, with overnight money trading at 13.0/14.0 percent in the morning. Overnight swap was at 0.6/0.7 and tom/next at 0.47/0.55. One-month swaps were at 12.50/13.25, two at 25.0/26.0, three at 37.5/38.0 and six at 75.25/75.75 points.
The central bank lowered its intervention band by one point to 2,407/2,599 and the conversion band also by one point to 2,407/2,455 on Friday.
